liveProbe.note: W783: this is the FROZEN 2026-09-10 capture of the retired engine (10 tools) and is deliberately NOT rewritten. The TypeScript host now serves 23 tools; the delta is declared in the *Delta blocks below.

w783Delta.why: The model needs to ask the user a question mid-turn. The answer arrives through POST /api/questions/{id}/answer (NOT /api/turn, which would be steering that a parked tool call never drains) and reaches the model as an ordinary tool_result.
w783Delta.notInRust: The retired engine has no counterpart: /api/tools there answered 10 tools and this tool did not exist.

w804Delta.why: The model needs to look at a local image (or a user-uploaded attachment by id) and have a vision-capable model actually see it; read_file is UTF-8 text only and rejects binary.
w804Delta.optionalMount: builtinTools mounts read_image only when the host supplies a session attachment store; the default registry of record stays the 7 contract tools.
w804Delta.endpoints: P0 adds ZERO endpoints: uploads ride POST /api/turn as inline base64 (attachment refs only in the log), so API_ENDPOINT_COUNT stays 51.

w7Delta.why: The orchestration face needs a relay named for what it does (send_message) and a stop switch that halts a worker without deleting it (STOPPED terminal; row + session kept for audit).
w7Delta.notInRust: The retired engine had neither the rename nor stop_worker.
w7Delta.endpoints: W7 adds ZERO endpoints: stop_worker rides the existing worker tool dispatch, so API_ENDPOINT_COUNT stays 51.

w884Delta.why: Progressive disclosure for skills (W882 discovery + the W874/W879 non-system-prompt decision): the model must be able to load ONE skill's SKILL.md body on demand. The catalog (name + description only) is injected as durable user-role history at every turn start; the body enters the conversation only when this tool is called. Read-only: no writes, no process, no network; the name goes through W882's name contract (no path traversal).
w884Delta.executionKeepList: W884 also adds load_skill to EXECUTION_TOOL_NAMES: it is a pure read and is NOT in SDK_TOOLS, so folding it would make skills unreachable in execution mode while the catalog still advertises them.
w884Delta.endpoints: W884 adds ZERO endpoints: the catalog rides the existing turn-start context lane and the tool rides the existing dispatch, so API_ENDPOINT_COUNT stays 61.

w1533Delta.why: The model needs a todo list the user can watch. Publishing it as a TOOL puts the list in the session log twice (the call's args and the result's tasks), so the panel restores it on refresh with no new data file, no new endpoint and no new service.
w1533Delta.semantics: REPLACE, not patch: every call carries the COMPLETE list, so two concurrent updates cannot merge into a state neither author intended. The result is {ok, tasks, counts:{pending,inProgress,completed}}.
w1533Delta.executionKeepList: W1533 also adds update_tasks to EXECUTION_TOOL_NAMES: it is not in SDK_TOOLS, so folding it would make the plan unreachable in execution mode while the user still expects to watch it (the same rule as W884 load_skill / F4 browser / B2 memory).
w1533Delta.endpoints: W1533 adds ZERO endpoints: the list rides the existing tool dispatch and the existing tool/tool_result SSE frames, so API_ENDPOINT_COUNT stays 69.

phase2Delta.why: trimContext and compactSession are both LOSSY AND UNAUTHORSIZED by the model: trim drops history with no record of what was dropped, and compactSession REWRITES the log. Phase 2 gives the model a derived-view compression it drives itself: compress replaces a closed range of turns with one summary block in the VIEW (the log keeps every event), decompress puts a block back, and context_status reports what is currently compressed and how full the context is.
phase2Delta.semantics: TURN-RANGE, turn-id based: {from_turn,to_turn} is a CLOSED interval over turn-<n> and is the only stable anchor (a Message has no id, a SessionEvent has no ordinal id, and the tool_call accumulator makes message<->event non-1:1). The engine hard-validates: the range must be turn-boundary aligned, both turns must exist, and to_turn MUST BE STRICTLY LESS THAN the current turn - compressing the turn in flight is refused by the engine, not by this description. Re-compressing a range that already covers a block MERGES (the old summary is consumed: a summary of summaries). decompress takes one block's {from_turn,to_turn} and restores the raw turns. None of the three writes a session event: the block list lives in <session-dir>/compression.json.
phase2Delta.executionKeepList: All three also join EXECUTION_TOOL_NAMES: none is in SDK_TOOLS, so folding them would make compression unreachable in execution mode while the system prompt still tells the model it has the tool (the same rule as W884 load_skill / W1533 update_tasks).
phase2Delta.endpoints: Phase 2 adds ZERO endpoints: all three ride the existing tool dispatch and the existing tool/tool_result SSE frames, and the block count / ranges / water level reach the host through the existing context_usage surface and the context_status result, so API_ENDPOINT_COUNT stays 69.

swarmDelta.sourceRef: packages/swarm/src/tool.ts (W-swarm; no Rust counterpart; design in docs/feature-agent-swarm.md)
swarmDelta.why: spawn_worker starts ONE resident collaboration session. When the work is instead a BATCH of 2-128 homogeneous subtasks that each want a fresh context, fanning them out one spawn_worker call per item is both slow and wrong: every member would become a resident row with its own report file, receipt and mailbox, and the main session would spend its own context merging N receipts. agent_swarm expands ONE call into a parallel batch of LIGHTWEIGHT turns, throttles them, and returns the whole batch as one structured result. The two coexist by design: resident collaboration stays with spawn_worker, batch homogeneous work comes here.
swarmDelta.semantics: BATCH, one-shot, no persistent state: each member is a fresh lightweight turn (own Context + in-memory session log) that is never registered in the worker registry and never writes a receipt file, so an interrupted batch is cancelled rather than resumed. Exactly four parameters plus the universal optional desc UI label: description (one line naming the batch), prompt_template (must contain the literal {{item}} placeholder), items (2-128 non-empty strings) and model (optional batch-level routing resolved by name; absent inherits the current session's model, and an unresolvable name is a STRUCTURED ERROR, never a silent fallback). Six hard validations run BEFORE any member starts - item count bounds, template presence, the {{item}} placeholder, non-empty items, and that expanding the template yields pairwise-distinct prompts - and a batch that fails them returns {ok:false, step:"validate", error} as a RESULT, not an exception, so the model can correct itself. A batch is also EXCLUSIVE: in one assistant reply agent_swarm must be the only tool call, because nothing in that reply's context is relevant to any member.
swarmDelta.executionKeepList: agent_swarm also joins EXECUTION_TOOL_NAMES: it is an ORCHESTRATION tool and is NOT in SDK_TOOLS, so folding it would make it unreachable in execution mode - the same "prompt must not lie" rule that kept load_skill (W884), the browser pair (F4), the memory write pair (B2), update_tasks (W1533) and the compression trio (W1900).
swarmDelta.endpoints: agent_swarm adds ZERO endpoints: the call rides the existing tool dispatch and the existing tool/tool_result SSE frames, and the member roster is pure in-memory progress surfaced by the host on the EXISTING statusline surface as an optional field, so API_ENDPOINT_COUNT stays 70.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. Send one or more questions, each with a stable id that will be echoed in the answer. The call PAUSES until the user answers, then returns `{answers:[{id,selected,custom}],timed_out:false}` as an ordinary tool result and you continue. If you recommend one option, put it first and append "（推荐）" to that label. The user may always type a free-text answer instead of choosing. Waiting is bounded (default 300000 ms, overridable with `timeout_ms`): on expiry the call returns `{answers:[],timed_out:true}` and NO choice is made for you — do not ask the same question again; state the assumption you are proceeding on (or stop and report) and continue with your own judgement.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

detail.description: Optional supporting detail shown with the question. Kept out of the option labels, so it never takes part in label matching.

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "（推荐）" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

intent.description: Optional presentation intent. It changes how a capable UI renders the question, never the answer encoding; a UI that does not know the tag shows the generic option list.

approve.description: The option label that approves the plan; every other option declines it.

timeout_ms.description: Optional maximum wait in milliseconds for the whole batch. Default 300000; capped at 3600000. On expiry the call returns an empty answer set with timed_out:true.

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: browser_act
tools.description: Act on the page opened by browser_open: click, type into, press a key on, or scroll an element identified by its stable ref from the last snapshot. Returns the updated accessibility snapshot and screenshot. Like browser_open, this call runs with RLIMIT_AS EXEMPTED (virtual address space unbounded) and reports the isolation state in its result.

action.description: What to do: click an element, type text into it, press a key, or scroll it.

ref.description: Stable ref from the last snapshot (required for click/type/scroll).

key.description: Key name for action=key, e.g. Enter, Tab, Escape.

delta_x.description: Horizontal scroll delta in pixels (action=scroll; default 0).

delta_y.description: Vertical scroll delta in pixels (action=scroll; default 0).

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: browser_open
tools.description: Open an absolute http(s) URL in a session-scoped headless browser and return the page's accessibility snapshot (interactive elements with stable refs) plus a PNG screenshot. Use those refs with browser_act. Requires the session's network capability (the sandbox must share the host network so the DevTools endpoint is reachable) and a session attachment store for the screenshot. This call runs with RLIMIT_AS EXEMPTED: the browser's virtual address space is NOT bounded by the sandbox, because Chromium cannot start under an address-space cap. Every other sandbox limit and the exact isolation state are reported in the result's isolation block.

viewport.description: Optional viewport size in CSS pixels (default 800x600).

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: forget
tools.description: Retract a previously remembered fact by its `id` (as returned by `remember`) or by its exact `text`. This APPENDS a tombstone to the workspace's append-only memory log — history is never rewritten, the entry is hidden from future turns. Only entries in this workspace's GLOBAL memory layer can be forgotten; a project-layer MEMORY.md is read-only. The result reports the layer, the absolute file, and the id retired.

id.description: Entry id to retract (as returned by remember).

text.description: Exact text of the entry to retract (alternative to id).

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: http_request
tools.description: Send an HTTP(S) request and return {status, headers(subset), body, truncated}. Only http/https URLs are allowed (file:// etc. rejected); redirects are followed up to 5 hops; the response body is truncated at 1MB (truncated:true beyond). HTTP error statuses are preserved in `status` — not tool errors; transport failures are categorized as timeout | dns | connect | redirect | invalid_url | invalid_arg | target_forbidden. SSRF policy: when CELESTEA_HTTP_ALLOW / CELESTEA_HTTP_DENY (comma-separated IP/CIDR) are set, every resolved target IP — and every redirect hop — must pass them; default (unset) allows all hosts.

url.description: Target URL; only http/https schemes are allowed.

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: list_dir
tools.description: List the entry names in a directory.

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: load_skill
tools.description: Load one skill's full instructions (its SKILL.md BODY) into the conversation by name. The per-turn skill catalog lists the available names; call this before doing a task a skill covers. The result carries the skill's `body`, its `dir` (read anything the body references from there with read_file), and the `source` layer it won — a skill's child files (references/, scripts/) are NEVER inlined. An unknown name, a name that is not a lowercase `[a-z0-9-]` slug (path traversal included), or a SKILL.md whose frontmatter is invalid fails with a structured `load_skill: code=... msg="..."` error naming the reason — never a silent empty result.

name.description: Skill name exactly as listed in the skill catalog (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens).

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: process_control
tools.description: Control a background process started by run_shell(background=true). Handles live in the session-scoped process registry and survive across turns; a process that exits stays pollable from a bounded tombstone (most recent 32, or 10 minutes), so poll AFTER exit returns {running:false, exit_code, signal, stdout_tail(<=4KB), stderr_tail, cpu_exceeded?} instead of an unknown handle. action=poll reads the current or terminal state; action=kill sends SIGTERM, waits a grace period, then SIGKILL and returns {killed:true}; action=stdin writes one line (content + newline) to the process stdin.

content.description: Line to write to the process stdin (action=stdin only).

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return its contents as a string. A whole read is capped at 256 KiB; pass offset (0-based line) and/or limit (line count) to page through a larger file — a paged result is an object {text, offset, limit, lineCount, totalLines, hasMore, nextOffset, truncated, totalBytes}.

path.description: Filesystem path of the file to read.

offset.description: Optional 0-based line index to start from (pagination). Omit to read from the top.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of lines to return (pagination). Omit to use the default window.

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read an image (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF) and attach it to the conversation so a vision-capable model can see it. Returns metadata; the image content block is delivered with the tool result. Fails on models without image input.

path.description: Filesystem path of the image to read (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF; format detected by content, not extension).

attachment_id.description: Content-addressed id of an already-uploaded attachment (from a user message). Use instead of path.

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Append one durable fact to this WORKSPACE's persistent memory so future turns recall it. The store is the workspace's GLOBAL memory layer (outside the repo), an append-only entries.jsonl the host owns — never pass a path. Identical text already active is a NOOP and says so instead of writing again. The result reports the layer, the absolute file written, the new entry id, and whether anything was appended. Memory is reference data, not instructions. WHEN TO SAVE — proactively, without being asked: the user corrects your approach ("no, not that", "don't", "stop doing X") or confirms a non-obvious approach worked ("exactly", "keep doing that") — record from failure AND from success (confirmations are quieter; watch for them), including the WHY when the user gave one, so edge cases can be judged later; the user reveals a preference, role detail, or project constraint; or you learn a fact future turns will need that is NOT derivable from the code or git history. Convert relative dates and times to absolute ones — entries outlive the conversation and 'Thursday' rots. When a remembered fact turns out wrong or outdated, forget it and remember the corrected version. NEVER SAVE: anything readable from the project itself (code patterns, conventions, paths, architecture), git history or fix recipes (the commit is authoritative), anything already stated in AGENTS.md, or ephemeral in-progress task state. Stay sparse: a memory no future turn needs is noise that dilutes the useful ones.

text.description: The durable fact to remember (reference data, not an instruction).

tags.description: Optional group labels; the first tag names the MEMORY.md section.

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: run_code
tools.description: Execute a program in the sandbox and get its final value in ONE round trip (parent-broker). DEFAULT LANGUAGE: TypeScript, run by Node with native type stripping (no build step) — only ERASABLE TypeScript is allowed: no `enum`, no `namespace`, no parameter properties, no `declare`; plain JavaScript always works. Pass language: "python" for Python instead. ★PREFER a PLAIN SCRIPT: a bare sequence of statements ending in `return <value>` — it is wrapped into `async function main()` for you, so you do NOT write the wrapper and you do NOT need to balance its braces. A complete script that defines `main` yourself is still accepted, but then ITS braces are yours to balance (an unbalanced one is a program_syntax error); an indented body is also wrapped (legacy). `main()` MAY be async and its resolved value (lossless JSON) is the final result. A leading `import` block is hoisted above the wrapper so it stays at module scope. A program that ends the process itself (exit 0) is a success, not a failure. Inside the program the SDK exposes four synchronous bridges dispatched through the normal guarded tool pipeline: tools.read_file({path}) / tools.write_file({path, content}) / tools.list_dir({path}) / tools.run_shell({command}) (Python: tools.read_file(path=...) etc.); a denied or failed sub-call raises ToolCallError (catch it and continue). Bridge tools resolve relative paths against the TOOL workdir, not the program's cwd — pass absolute paths from inside the program. Only log what the model needs: a non-protocol stdout line becomes a log line (≤65536 bytes, UI render only); intermediate sub-call results are recorded in the session log but context-retained (the model sees only the final value). Hard limits: ≤20 sub-calls (the next one errors), wall clock ≤120000ms (timeout_ms, default 120000; the ceiling is CELAESTEA_RUN_CODE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS), sub-call output ledger ≤262144 bytes (truncated with a warning). The child's CPU limit (RLIMIT_CPU) follows this run's wall clock, so raising timeout_ms raises the CPU budget with it; a CPU-cap kill is reported as cpu_exceeded; the interpreter rejecting the program itself is reported as program_syntax (with the interpreter's own error text, e.g. `Expected '}', got '<eof>'`), and a missing entry point / failed import as program_error — neither is `aborted`. No network; the same sandbox as run_shell (bwrap/raw/userspace + rlimits).

language.description: Program language; default "typescript". TypeScript runs under Node's native type stripping (erasable syntax only: no enum/namespace/parameter properties) and needs no build; "python" runs under python3 -uB.

code.description: Program source in the chosen language. RECOMMENDED: a bare sequence of statements ending in `return <value>` — the engine wraps it into `async function main()` for you (do NOT write the wrapper; there are no braces for you to balance). Also accepted: a complete script that defines `main` yourself, in which case you own its braces. The engine injects the SDK preamble (tools bridge + protocol).

timeout_ms.description: Optional whole-run wall clock in ms. Default 120000; the hard cap is CELAESTEA_RUN_CODE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (default 120000, so it is unchanged unless the deployer raises it). CELAESTEA_RUN_CODE_TIMEOUT_MS tunes the default, never the cap. The child's CPU limit follows this value.

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: run_shell
tools.description: Run a shell command inside the sandbox (v2 OS isolation when available: namespaces + read-only root + resource limits, else the v1 userspace path; fixed workdir, sanitized env, bounded timeout and output) and return stdout, stderr, exit code, and a `sandbox` object {provider: bwrap|raw|userspace, net_isolated, tmp_private, seccomp, enforcement, promise_gaps} reporting the effective isolation — READ promise_gaps before trusting any resource claim: a host with no rlimit mechanism lists the token rlimits there, and on such a host cpu_sec is NOT enforced (the result says so with cpu_cap_enforced:false) (W249: network isolated and /tmp a private tmpfs by default; CELESTEA_SANDBOX_NET=1 / CELESTEA_SANDBOX_SHARE_TMP=1 restore the shared host net/tmp; CELESTEA_SANDBOX_SECCOMP=1 enables the seccomp whitelist). With background:true the command is spawned detached (no call-level timeout; resource limits still apply) and returns {background, handle, pid} immediately — control it with the process_control tool (poll / stdin / kill); background processes live in the session process registry and survive across turns. Default timeout is 30s; raise it with timeout_ms up to the cap configured by CELESTEA_SHELL_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (default 300000ms). The CPU limit (RLIMIT_CPU) FOLLOWS this call's wall clock unless cpu_sec is given: a foreground call gets its effective timeout rounded up plus 5s of grace, while background:true — which has no call-level wall clock — gets the cap itself (CELESTEA_SHELL_MAX_CPU_SEC, default 600). Optional cpu_sec overrides RLIMIT_CPU for THIS process; values above that cap are CLAMPED to it, and a CPU-cap kill is reported as cpu_exceeded.

workdir.description: Optional working directory. Must already exist inside the sandbox root; relative paths resolve against the sandbox workdir.

timeout_ms.description: Optional per-call timeout in milliseconds. Default 30000; can be raised up to the cap from CELESTEA_SHELL_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (default 300000). When cpu_sec is not given this is also what the CPU limit follows. Ignored when background:true.

cpu_sec.description: Optional per-call CPU time limit in seconds for THIS process. It is applied as RLIMIT_CPU **only when the host actually has a rlimit mechanism** (Linux with prlimit, or a shell with usable ulimit builtins); on a host without one the value is still reported back as sandbox.cpu_sec but NOT enforced, and the result carries sandbox.promise_gaps including "rlimits" — so read that field rather than assuming the cap bit. Without cpu_sec the limit follows the call: a foreground call gets its effective timeout_ms rounded up plus 5s of grace, while background:true (no call-level wall clock) gets CELESTEA_SHELL_MAX_CPU_SEC (default 600). Values above that cap are clamped to it. When the cap really is in force and the kernel sends SIGXCPU, the result reports cpu_exceeded:true naming the limit.

background.description: Optional, default false. When true, spawn the command detached (no call-level timeout, so the CPU limit defaults to the CELESTEA_SHELL_MAX_CPU_SEC cap unless cpu_sec is given) and return {background:true, handle, pid} immediately; control the process with process_control (poll / stdin / kill). A process that exits stays pollable from a bounded tombstone (most recent 32, or 10 minutes), so poll after exit still returns exit_code/signal and the tails.

notify.description: Optional, default true. When background:true, whether a NATURAL exit may be offered to a host completion sink. No sink is wired in this deployment, so read the terminal state with process_control(action=poll); the flag is kept for hosts that install one.

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: spawn_worker
tools.description: 在 harness 内拉起一个 worker 会话：创建子会话（可入工作区分组）→ 命名（标题=<wid>·<短名>）→ 指定模型 → 投递自包含简报。worker 由 harness 自己的 agent-loop 驱动；看门狗按 registry 判定存活并自动重派失败项。wid 是 worker 编号（如 W101）；brief 是自包含任务简报文本。返回 {ok, sessionId, title, wid}。协作闭环：worker 完成后引擎自动写报告 results/<wid>-<short>.md 并发送 WORKER_<wid>_DONE/FAILED 回执到 report_to 目标会话；回执到达会唤醒目标会话的新一轮处理（主 agent 读报告整合结论）。spawn 后应等待回执到达或经 worker_status 查询进度，再整合各 worker 结论。 mode 是可选的工作方式（缺省继承父会话）；worker 报告头部会写明 mode。

title.description: 会话标题短名（不含 wid· 前缀，≤20 字；缺省取简报首行/文件名）

workspace.description: 工作区/项目根目录（cwd 分组；缺省 harness 工作区）

provider.description: 模型 provider（缺省取 harness 默认）

model.description: 模型名（缺省取 harness 默认）

mode.description: worker 会话的会话模式（W729）：缺省继承父会话的 mode；standard=逐步直调工具，execution=优先用一个 run_code 程序完成多步依赖调用

permission.description: worker 子会话的权限预设（W9）：read-only / write-read / full-access 或自定义预设 id；缺省继承 host 的权限解析（未设置=full-access）。落到子会话 meta 与 registry 行的 permission= token。

tools.name: update_tasks
tools.description: Publish the CURRENT task list for this session (a todo list the user watches). Send the COMPLETE list every time: it REPLACES the previous one, so never send a diff or a single changed row. Each item is {content, status}, where status is 'pending' (not started), 'in_progress' (being worked on now) or 'completed' (finished and verified) — mark an item completed only when the work is actually done. Use it when a request needs several steps: write the list first, keep at most ONE item in_progress, and re-send the whole list as you go. The result echoes the normalized list and its counts as {ok, tasks, counts:{pending,inProgress,completed}}; an empty tasks array clears the list. An item with a blank content or an unknown status fails with a structured `update_tasks: code=... msg="..."` error and changes nothing.

tasks.description: The COMPLETE task list, in display order. Replaces the previous list; an empty array clears it.

content.description: One-line description of the task, in the user's language.

status.description: pending = not started, in_progress = being worked on now, completed = finished and verified.

tools.name: compress
tools.description: Replace a CLOSED RANGE of earlier turns with one summary block, so the same information costs far fewer context tokens. This is a tool, not an obligation: compress only when the context is genuinely getting full (context_status tells you), and only a COLD range - never the turn you are answering in. Send {from_turn, to_turn} as turn numbers (turn numbers are the log's own ids, so the FIRST turn of a session is turn 0; context_status lists exactly these numbers), never message numbers or indexes. The engine refuses a range that does not line up with turn boundaries, a turn that does not exist, or any range whose to_turn is the current turn or later. Write the summary for your own future self: what was decided, what was learned, what is still open, and where the evidence is (file paths, ids, commands) - not a transcript and not a narration of what you are doing now. The history is not deleted: the log keeps every original event, and if the summary turns out to be wrong or insufficient you can call decompress with the same range to get the original turns back. Re-compressing a range that already contains a block merges into it (your summary then replaces the old one, so carry its still-relevant content forward). The result is {ok:true, block:{from_turn,to_turn,summary,created_turn,context_ratio}, merged:<how many earlier blocks were absorbed>}; a refused range returns a structured error naming the reason and changes nothing.

from_turn.description: First turn of the range to compress, as a turn NUMBER (0 = the first turn of this session; these are the log's own turn ids). Inclusive.

to_turn.description: Last turn of the range to compress. Inclusive, MUST be strictly less than the current turn (the turn in flight cannot be compressed), and must be a turn the log actually has. Use context_status to see the numbers.

summary.description: The replacement text, written for your own future self: decisions made, facts learned with their evidence (paths, ids, commands), open questions, and anything you must not forget. It is the only trace of those turns you will have in the view, so do not write a narration or a transcript, and do not leave out the details you would otherwise have to re-derive.

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: decompress
tools.description: Undo a compress: the original turns of one block go back into the view, in full, exactly as they were (nothing was ever deleted from the log - compression only changed what the model sees). Compression is meant to be reversible, so a summary that lost a detail you need is a normal situation and not a failure: call decompress with the block's own {from_turn,to_turn} and read the original turns again. Pass a range that matches NO current block and nothing changes. Note the cost: the restored turns take their tokens back, so decompress the smallest block that has what you are missing rather than everything, and re-compress it afterwards if you no longer need it. The result is {ok:true, from_turn, to_turn, restored_turns:<how many turns came back>}; a range with no block returns {ok:false, code:'no_such_block'} and changes nothing.

from_turn.description: First turn of the block to restore - the from_turn of an existing compress call. Inclusive.

to_turn.description: Last turn of the block to restore - the to_turn of that same compress call. Inclusive.

desc.description: Optional one-line label (max 80 chars) describing what this call is doing; shown on the tool card in the UI. Keep it short.

tools.name: context_status
tools.description: Report how full this session's context is, and what is currently compressed. Read-only: it changes nothing. Use it when you are unsure whether to compress (that is the normal case - compression is a tool, not a routine) and before you pick a range. The result is {context:{used,window,ratio,method,estimated,projected}, turn:{current,turns}, blocks:[{from_turn,to_turn,created_turn,context_ratio,summary_chars}], current_turn}. Every turn number here is a log id: turn-0 is the first turn of the session, and these are the same numbers compress and decompress take. method is 'usage_prompt_tokens' when the provider reported a real prompt size, 'assembled_estimate' when the figure is an estimate of the request that would be sent now, and 'none' before anything has been generated. ratio is used/window and is the number to weigh your decision against: 0.5 is the point where a cold range is worth compressing, 0.8 is where the engine starts insisting. The ranges in blocks are exactly the ranges decompress accepts.

tools.name: agent_swarm
tools.description: Run one BATCH of 2-128 homogeneous subtasks in PARALLEL and get the whole batch back in a single result. Use it when the work splits into many same-shaped pieces that each want their own fresh context ("summarise these 30 files", "apply this fix to every module under packages/") - NOT for resident collaboration, which stays with spawn_worker. There is no spawn-per-item cost: every member is a LIGHTWEIGHT turn with its own context, registered nowhere and writing no report file, so an interrupted batch is cancelled rather than resumed. How to call it: give a one-line description of the whole batch, a prompt_template containing the literal {{item}} placeholder, and items (2-128 non-empty strings) as the per-member variable - the template is expanded once per item, and the same template runs for every item, so it must be self-contained: a member shares none of this reply's context and none of its siblings'. The batch is EXCLUSIVE: agent_swarm must be the ONLY tool call in your reply, because nothing in that reply's context is relevant to any member; if you also need another tool, do it in a separate turn. Six checks run BEFORE any member starts - item count in range, a template when there are items, the {{item}} placeholder present, every item non-empty, and every expanded prompt distinct - and a failed check comes back as a structured result you can correct and retry, never an exception. Optional model routes the whole batch by model name and inherits the current session's model when omitted; a name that does not resolve is a structured error, not a silent downgrade. Results arrive as one XML block whose <summary> gives the per-state counts and whose <subagent> entries are numbered from 1 in YOUR items order (not completion order), each carrying its state, its outcome and its escaped text - that block is the authority on what happened, so read it before answering. Members that hit provider rate limits are retried with jittered backoff, and the concurrency cap holds regardless, so a large batch will not stampede a provider.

description.description: One short line naming the whole batch (shown as the batch's label in the UI). Keep it under 80 chars.

prompt_template.description: The prompt every member runs, with the literal {{item}} placeholder where the per-member text is substituted. The same template runs for every item, so it must be self-contained.

items.description: The per-member variable: 2 to 128 non-empty strings, each trimmed non-empty. One member per item; two items that expand to the same prompt are refused.
One member's worth of work: a file path, a symbol name, a subject line - whatever {{item}} stands for in your template.

model.description: Optional model for the WHOLE batch, resolved by registered model name; omit it to inherit the current session's model. A name that does not resolve is reported as a structured error, never silently downgraded.
